title: The Deutsch–Jozsa Algorithm
summary: Decide constant or balanced for an n-bit function with one query.
objectives: Extend Deutsch's circuit to an n-bit input register with Hadamard gates before and after the oracle
Read the outcome: |0…0⟩ means constant, any other result means balanced
Compare the one quantum query with the 2^(n−1) + 1 queries a deterministic classical algorithm needs
mission: Call oracle(qc) once so that the input register (qubits 0 to 2) ends in |000⟩ if the hidden function is constant, and has zero probability of being |000⟩ if it is balanced.

prediction.question: A deterministic classical algorithm must decide, with no error, whether a function of 3 bits is constant or balanced. How many queries does it need in the worst case?
prediction.explanation: If the first 4 queries return the same value, the function can still be balanced, so only the fifth query decides. In general the worst case is 2^(n−1) + 1 queries. The quantum algorithm uses one.

hints: Prepare the auxiliary qubit in |−⟩ as in the phase kickback lesson: qc.x(3), then qc.h(3).
Apply a Hadamard to qubits 0, 1 and 2 before the oracle, and again after it.
qc.x(3), qc.h(3), Hadamard on qubits 0 to 2, oracle(qc), Hadamard on qubits 0 to 2.
